brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact but CoWoS remains binding constraint; SK Hynix HBM4 share advantage widens over Samsung
brief.summary: <cite index="11-2,14-1">DRAM contract pricing surged 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, with NAND up 70-75%, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM jump.</cite> <cite index="21-5,25-6">Hyperscaler capex is tracking $600-725B in 2026 (+36% YoY), with ~75% ($450B+) dedicated to AI infrastructure.</cite> <cite index="3-18,3-27">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market at $54.6B (+58% YoY), with UBS projecting SK Hynix to hold ~70% share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform versus Samsung's delayed qualification.</cite> <cite index="31-4,34-2">TSMC CoWoS capacity is scaling from 35K to 120-130K wafers/month by end-2026, but all three backend fabs remain fully booked with 52-78 week lead times, creating a compound bottleneck with HBM3E allocation.</cite> <cite index="1-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit persisting in 2026 despite fab expansions.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs. short Samsung Electronics. SK Hynix maintains decisive HBM qualification advantage (HBM3E and early HBM4 volume ramp with TSMC packaging partnership secured), while Samsung still battles yield/qualification delays despite incremental HBM4 announcements. Memory ASP inflection favors purer-play exposure; Samsung's Device Solutions margin recovery lags Hynix given foundry/logic drag and later HBM4 revenue contribution. Spread has room to widen into Q3 earnings as Hynix confirms 2H26 HBM4 shipments to Nvidia/hyperscalers while Samsung's timing remains opaque. Risk: Samsung breakthrough on HBM4 qual or unexpected Hynix CoWoS allocation constraints.

memory_cycle.notes: Pricing momentum remains extreme (Q2 DRAM +58-63%, NAND +70-75% QoQ) but rate-of-change decelerating from Q1's unprecedented +90-95% DRAM spike. Supply deficit structural through 2027: HBM capacity-to-DDR5 conversion ratio (3:1) and hyperscaler LTAs locking 60%+ of leading-edge output. Legacy DRAM (DDR4/LPDDR4) seeing tightest conditions as majors phase out production. Spot pricing volatility rising; some accounts report 'hourly pricing' models emerging. New fab capacity (Samsung P5, Hynix M15X) delayed to 2H27-2028, offering no near-term relief. Cycle peak timing unclear but consensus expects elevated pricing into 2027-2028.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="3-18,3-19">BofA pegs 2026 HBM market at $54.6B (+58% YoY), with Goldman forecasting HBM demand for custom ASIC chips surging 82%, accounting for one-third of the market.</cite> <cite index="3-27">UBS projects SK Hynix capturing ~70% of HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin in 2026.</cite> <cite index="34-13,34-14">HBM3E 8-hi and 12-hi stacks fully allocated for 2026, with prices up 15-22% YoY; SK Hynix (50% market share) signals shortages extending into late 2027.</cite> <cite index="8-3,43-3">Samsung expanding HBM capacity ~50% in 2026; P5 fab operational 2028, while SK Hynix's M15X targets mid-2027.</cite> Intel and SoftBank pursuing ZAM (Zero-Angle Memory) as post-HBM alternative with 2-3x bandwidth vs. HBM3, targeting 2029 commercialization, but near-term irrelevant. Supply remains the gating factor—not demand.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix maintains HBM3E/HBM4 dual-generation leadership, secures 70% Nvidia Rubin share per UBS
news_pulse.implication: Reinforces Hynix's qualification moat and TSMC packaging partnership. BofA/UBS both naming Hynix as top pick in memory supercycle. Samsung still playing catch-up on HBM4 despite recent announcements.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND +70-75%; TrendForce cites AI server demand and CSP LTAs
news_pulse.implication: Pricing power remains exceptional but momentum slowing from Q1's +90-95% DRAM surge. Confirms memory suppliers maintaining discipline; no panic capacity adds. Consumer segments (PC DRAM, client SSDs) facing harshest supply constraints.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex revised up to $725B in 2026 (Meta $125-145B, Amazon ~$200B, Alphabet $175-185B, MSFT $120B+)
news_pulse.implication: Sustained AI buildout validates multi-year memory demand. Meta citing 'higher component pricing' as driver of $10B capex raise signals memory inflation cascading into hyperscaler budgets. Demand-side risk remains negligible.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity scaling to 120-130K wpm by end-2026 (from 35K in late 2024), but all lines sold out with 52-78 week lead times
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging remains the true bottleneck—even if HBM and logic wafers available, cannot ship without CoWoS. Nvidia locked 60-70% of capacity for B200/Rubin. Substrate/OSAT layer (Amkor, SPIL) also constrained. Samsung/Intel packaging alternatives (I-Cube, Foveros) not yet scaled.

news_pulse.headline: Goldman: 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026; memory shortage may persist until 2027-2028 per multiple sources
news_pulse.implication: Supply deficit structural, not cyclical. HBM's 3:1 wafer consumption ratio vs. DDR5 means each HBM ramp further compresses commodity DRAM. New fabs (Samsung P5, Hynix M15X) don't contribute until 2027-2028, limiting relief.

news_pulse.headline: Nanya Tech: DDR4/LPDDR4 shortage limiting DDR5 shift; GM says DRAM margins across all segments now top HBM
news_pulse.implication: Legacy DRAM seeing explosive pricing as majors (Samsung, Hynix, Micron) phase out DDR4 for HBM/DDR5. Tier-2 players like Nanya benefiting from 3-year LTAs. Suggests even non-HBM DRAM highly profitable in current environment—supports broad-based margin expansion thesis.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix shifting Cheongju mask fab toward HBM yield push; M15X mega-fab dedicated entirely to next-gen memory
news_pulse.implication: Hynix doubling down on HBM capacity and backend integration. Cheongju M15X (size of 32 soccer fields) targeting late-2027 ramp entirely for HBM/advanced DRAM. Reinforces multi-year supply tightness and Hynix's willingness to allocate capital aggressively.

news_pulse.headline: CNBC: Memory stocks (Samsung +114% YTD, SK Hynix +186%, Micron +141%) face cyclicality risk warnings from BlueBox, Ranmore
news_pulse.implication: Valuation/momentum concerns emerging after YTD rally. Cautious voices argue sector hasn't structurally escaped cyclicality and current pricing assumes sustained discipline. Nomura still bullish (Hynix 4M won, Samsung 590K won 12-mo targets). Near-term risk: profit-taking or rotation, but fundamentals remain intact.

brief.derivatives_signal: Options flow unavailable in payload. ADR/OTC pricing not provided. Monitor KOSPI 200 futures (KS200=F) for beta/sentiment proxy. Single-stock leveraged ETFs for Samsung/Hynix listing May 27 on KRX (18 products, 43.2T won planned size)—watch for retail vol spike and basis risk in futures-based products. Hong Kong-listed Samsung/Hynix 2x leveraged ETFs reportedly hold 2.4T/7.9T won AUM; cross-border flow could amplify intraday moves. If accessible, fade short-dated OTM calls on rallies given momentum crowding warnings from sell-side. Prefer Hynix vs. Samsung in any paired structure.

TSMC CoWoS allocation commentary or OSAT (Amkor/SPIL) capacity announcements (binding constraint for both names)
Hyperscaler earnings call transcripts for incremental capex/memory pricing color (Meta/Amazon/MSFT already reported; watch for revisions)
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price updates (contract pricing lagging spot by 2-4 weeks; spot weakness would be early warning)
Korean construction/materials stocks (SK ecoplant, Samsung C&T) for fab buildout progress signals (leading indicator for 2027-2028 supply)
